newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo sales and profit trends by sector.
newsitem.headline: Akzo sales and profit trends by sector.

text.p: Dutch chemicals group Akzo Nobel on Thursday reported 1996 net income of 1.318 billion guilders, versus 1995's 1.314 billion.
It said its high-margin pharmaceuticals and coatings businesses booked higher 1996 resuts, while chemicals and fibres were down year-on-year.
It gave the following breakdown of sales and operating income per activity:
PHARMACEUTICALS

Sales up five percent at 3.95 billion guilders, reflecting a two percent increase in selling prices, a two percent contribution from currency exchange rates and one percent higher turnover due to acquisitions.
Prescription drugs unit Organon's results lagged 1995 due to lower results on contraceptive pills and costs of new product launches (fertility drug Puregon, anti-depressant Remeron).

But Akzo said this decline was more than offset by higher contributions to profits by other business units, particularly Intervet (veterinary products) and Diosynth (specialised raw materials for the pharmaceuticals industry).
COATINGS
Sales up nine percent at 7.44 million guilders, mainly due to currency (four percent) and higher selling prices (two percent).
* Acquisitions boost sales by three percent.
* Raw material prices fell from high 1995 levels.
* Operating income up at 592 million guilders from 474 million.
Decorative coatings books flat operating earnings.
Other business units outperform 1995, particularly Car Refinishes and Industrial Coatings.
CHEMICALS
Sales up five percent at Dfl 7.70 billion, reflecting positive effect from currencies (four pct) and higher volumes (two pct).
Selling prices down an average one percent year-on-year.
Major sales gains at Polymer Chemicals, Catalysts, Functional Chemicals and Salt America.
Vinyl chloride monomer (VCM) and PVC activities booked lower operating profits due to stagnant European PVC market.
Surface chemistry results also significantly lower.
These adverse effects partly offset by higher earnings at chlor-alkali activities and Functional chemicals.
Operating income for the sector fell five percent to 576 million guilders.
FIBRES
Fibre performance dragged down by very weak business climate but remained in positive figures during all four quarters.
Sales down one percent at 3.93 billion guilders, excluding four percent effect of packaging resins divestment.
Volumes up three percent.
Average selling prices down five percent.
Operating profits down to Dfl 82 million guilders from 158 million.
Biggest laggards were Textile Fibres, reflecting poor performance of viscose textiles, and Industrial Fibres, due to Brazilian operations.
Non-wovens hit by adverse trends in roofing sector.
Aramid Products and Membrana turn in improved performance.
